page.layout: One printed page, numbered 133, with a running head "PROROGANDA." at the top. One block of running text in a single column, with no margin notes and no notes below the text.

main_text.p: Apud Petragonos & Lemouicos castanea & rapa à vino & melle tertium honorem adpi-scebantur: rapa etiam Allobrogibus & Subaudis in cibis mirifice grata, sicut & castanea montanis Lugdunensibus fuere.

Montium Cemannorum populi Aruernis & Velleis proximi vice panificii vtebantur, & etiamnunc vtuntur castaneis, quippe festis tantum diebus, vel non infima sortis ac fortuna homines panificium illic ex frugibus vsurpant.

Gasconum gens Aquitaniæ nobilissima inter præcipua pulmentaria alia habet & cepas, quorū olfactum & gustatum in delitiis gula vertit & suauia condimenta: hi nunc quoq; pra cæteris Gallis ventri indulgere magis creduntur: vulgatum enim & maxime nobilitatum apud eos jactatur prouerbium, satius esse ventrem belle farcire epulis, quam corpus veste molli & pretiosa ornare, adjuntq; Burgundioni ventrem esse sericeum.

p.i: Nortmanni malis pyrisq; crudis ac coctis vē-scebantur liberaliter, suosq; ex illis concinnabant potus, carnibus praterea omnigenis vtebantur.

main_text.p: Narbonensis Gallia pisces habet frequentes, tum sale conditos, ante cuncta autem oleuas condi-tas capparesq; manducat, ficus item vuasq; recentes, mala citria, arantia, limones inter lautiores cibos habet & gula irritamenta: vina apud eos generosissima: oues pascuntur thymo, quo pabulo mire pinguefcunt.

page.notes: The text is faint and partly blotted, especially at the right edge and in the lower lines. Some letters in "vē-scebantur", "oleuas" and "pinguefcunt" are doubtful and may be printing or reading errors. The words "Armo-" at the foot appear to be a catchword; the page number 133 is printed at the head right. The line "13 Armo-" at the bottom contains a partial signature-like number that may be the catchword, and I have listed the catchword once only.
